title: Initiative: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (overload protection)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Reliability Program — Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding
description:
## Why this initiative exists
We are seeing repeated Sev1/Sev2 incidents and customer escalations during predictable traffic spikes (batch jobs, product launches, partner promotions). Current behavior under overload is often ambiguous 5xx/timeouts and tail-latency collapse, which drives retry storms and cascading failures across gateway → routing/control plane → runtime/GPU pools.

This initiative introduces layered circuit breakers + deterministic load shedding across the Hosted API request path.

## Outcomes / goals
1) Prevent cascading failures under overload
- Cap queue growth and shed earlier (edge when possible) before control plane or runtime collapses.
- Keep control plane responsive even during GPU pool saturation / regional brownouts.
- Avoid retry storms by returning stable, cacheable errors with explicit retry guidance.

2) Improve customer experience during overload
- Clear and consistent error semantics (HTTP + Redwood error codes) across REST + OpenAI-compat endpoints.
- Provide Retry-After and documented retry/backoff guidance.
- Where configured and safe, allow graceful degradation (fallback model/region/tier) instead of hard failure.

3) SLO alignment + observability
- Track overload-protected errors separately from internal failures for SLO/error budget accounting.
- Add end-to-end metrics, dashboards, and alerts tied to overload signals and breaker state transitions.

## Non-goals
- Replacing existing quotas / rate limits (this complements them).
- Major re-architecture of the runtime scheduler.
- Customer-specific bespoke overload logic beyond supported policy primitives.

## Scope (by layer)
### Edge / API gateway
- Admission control hook (tier/route/model, streaming vs non-streaming, request classification)
- Deterministic error mapping + headers (Retry-After)
- Feature flags for per-region/per-model rollout

### Routing / control plane
- Per-(model, region, tier) breaker state store + evaluation API
- Integrate capacity signals (GPU pool saturation, queue depth, error rate)
- Fallback interactions (policy engine guardrails to avoid unsafe loops)

### Runtime / data plane
- Bounded request queues + shed points at scheduler boundaries (prefill/decode)
- Memory pressure / KV-cache guardrails to shed before OOM and latency spirals
- Reason codes plumbed gateway → routing → runtime → logs/traces

### Customer-facing enablement
- Docs updates, console/status messaging patterns, support runbooks
- SDK behavior alignment (surface overload codes + Retry-After cleanly)

## Milestones (proposed → tracked here)
Phase 0 — Discovery (1–2 weeks)
- Identify top overload failure modes from incidents + metrics
- Draft error taxonomy + mapping + retry semantics
- Agree on “what counts for SLO” vs “overload-protected”

Phase 1 — Foundations (3–5 weeks)
- Implement core breaker primitives and bounded queues (behind flags)
- Baseline metrics and tracing for admission/shed/breaker transitions

Phase 2 — Policy + Degradation (3–6 weeks)
- Integrate routing capacity signals into breaker decisions
- Add fallback interactions + tier-aware behavior (Hosted vs Dedicated alignment)
- Guardrails to prevent unsafe customer configs

Phase 3 — Rollout + hardening (2–4 weeks)
- Canary in us-east for 1–2 models
- Game days and incident-bot enhancements
- Alert tuning + docs/support readiness
- Expand to more regions/models

## Success metrics
Reliability
- Reduce overload-driven Sev1/Sev2 incidents (target: meaningful reduction vs previous quarter baseline)
- Avoid control-plane brownouts during spikes (routing P99 latency stable under load)

Customer experience
- Decrease ambiguous 5xx/timeouts during overload; increase deterministic 429/503 with actionable codes
- SDKs surface Retry-After + overload reason codes; reduced “what does this 503 mean?” tickets

Performance
- Improved tail latency under overload conditions (p99 should degrade gracefully, not collapse)
- Runtime queue depth remains bounded; no runaway growth leading to multi-minute recovery

## Owners / stakeholders
SRE: Rafael Mendes (lead), Christine Wong (breaker implementation), Tomáš Novák (incident reduction)
Platform/Routing: Mina Haddad (lead), Ravi Menon (capacity integration), Jordan Lee (policy)
Runtime: Noah Patel (architect), Lena Fischer (bounded queues), Samir Qureshi (memory pressure)
Observability: Allison Grant (standards), Sergio Costa (dashboards)
Product: Nikhil Sharma, Henry Cho; Dedicated alignment: Lauren Bishop

## Rollout plan (high-level)
- Ship all changes behind feature flags with per-(region, model) enablement.
- Canary: us-east, low-risk model(s) first; monitor shed rate, p95/p99 latency, breaker flapping, and customer tickets.
- Gradual expansion by model class then region; add “kill switch” for emergency disable.
- Communicate externally once behavior is stable and docs/SDKs are ready (error semantics must be consistent across endpoints).

## Links (artifacts being produced under sub-issues)
- PRs (expected): gateway admission control, shared error schema, routing breaker state machine, runtime bounded queues, dashboard + SLO toolkit changes
- Docs: overload errors + retry guidance
- Runbooks + status page templates

## Open questions (tracked here until resolved)
- Final mapping: when do we return 429 vs 503 (tier-aware)?
- Retry-After defaults: static vs derived from breaker cooldown/recovery time?
- Streaming: shed points and semantics (disconnect vs structured terminal error); alignment with SDK behavior
- Dedicated alignment: where Dedicated differs (predictable capacity vs shedding) and how we message it
comments: 2025-10-28 — Talia Benson: Created umbrella to track cross-team execution. Please keep status updates here weekly; implementation details go in sub-issues.

2025-11-04 — Rafael Mendes: Phase 0 findings: top failure mode is queue blowup (gateway retries + runtime backlog) leading to multi-minute recovery. Second is control-plane latency increase causing routing timeouts. Action: prioritize bounded queues + early shed at gateway. Tracking taxonomy draft in ENG-4823; breaker state model in ENG-4824/4828.

2025-11-12 — Mina Haddad: Routing side: we need breaker evaluation to be cheap and resilient; prefer local cache + persisted state store with hysteresis. Also need a single “shed hint” propagated to gateway so edge can shed without hammering routing. Will coordinate API shape in ENG-4824/4825.

2025-11-18 — Henry Cho: Product note: customers care more about consistency than the specific code. We should commit to stable body shape + headers across REST and OpenAI-compat, and document retry guidance prominently. Please make sure SDKs surface Retry-After and Redwood error codes (ENG-4836).

2025-11-26 — Noah Patel: Runtime: bounded queues are feasible without scheduler rewrite, but we need to be explicit about shed points (enqueue vs prefill boundary vs decode). Streaming is tricky: we should prefer shedding before stream starts; once tokens flow, prefer completing if possible to avoid partial outputs. Capturing in ENG-4826/4827.

2025-12-09 — Sergio Costa: Draft dashboard panels ready for review: admission rate, shed rate by reason, breaker state transitions, runtime queue depth, p95/p99 latency, 429/503 breakdown by model/region/tier. Please confirm label cardinality constraints before we roll out to prod metrics. (ENG-4830/4829)

2025-12-16 — Rafael Mendes: Canary readiness checklist (us-east, 2 models) agreed with SRE + Platform. Need the emergency disable toggle (INT-1182 requested; also tracking flag controls in ENG-4834). Oncall paging rules need update so load-shedding doesn’t page as “hard failure” (ENG-4840 will tune post-canary).

2026-01-06 — Christine Wong: Canary data (week 1): breaker prevented queue runaway during two traffic spikes. Observed ~6–9% shed rate at peak, but p99 stabilized vs previous behavior (no multi-minute tail). One issue: breaker flapping during rapid recovery; hotfix in progress with additional cooldown regression test. Please watch for customer reports of increased 429s (support thread references SUP-3974).

2026-01-12 — Rafael Mendes: Next steps: (1) finalize Retry-After guidance based on observed recovery times; (2) expand canary to one additional region after flapping fix; (3) complete docs + SDK surfacing before broad rollout. Reminder: success for this initiative is reduced Sev1/Sev2 + fewer ambiguous 5xx/timeouts; not ‘zero shedding’. Post-launch review planned in ENG-4841.
